subject: Unscheduled stability safeguard activation and verification request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Unscheduled stability safeguard activation and verification request
Attachments: hotfix_patch_notes.pdf, verification_steps.txt

Hi team —

Quick note: our runtime on a small subset of multi-tenant inference pools has tripped a memory fragmentation pattern under a specific request mix. We’re not seeing data exposure or correctness issues; this is a stability risk that can lead to isolated OOMs and degraded latency on affected nodes.

We are scheduling an immediate, short unscheduled safeguard activation (hotfix) to enable a conservative allocator-mode and trigger an automatic memory compaction path. This is a rolling change with the goal of avoiding customer-facing downtime. Window: 09:30–10:00 PT (today). Expected impact: brief connection resets for inflight requests to affected hosts (under 30s per host), transparent failover to healthy hosts for autoscaled fleets.

What we need from you:
- Please run the attached verification steps after 10:00 PT (verification_steps.txt) and confirm whether you see any residual 5xx or OOM traces.
- If you have any long-running realtime sessions, please save state where possible before 09:30 PT.
- If you’re on Dedicated (reserved) capacity, note that we will apply the config on the host pool but will avoid capacity reboots unless absolutely required — we will call that out.

We’ll post real-time updates to the incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-9981 and the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/9981. I’ll post completion and the short postmortem follow-up in this thread.

Sorry for the short notice — Marissa (cc’d) is leading the fix; Stephanie is on standby for communications.

Next update: 09:35 PT with start confirmation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

--
Attachment stubs:
- hotfix_patch_notes.pdf (summary of allocator mode change, risk/caveats)
- verification_steps.txt (short smoke tests and log grep commands)
From: Acme Ops <ops@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T09:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled stability safeguard activation and verification request

Thanks Ben — appreciate the heads up. Two quick Qs: 1) Will this affect our dedicated inference pool (ACME-POOL-3)? 2) Any ETA on whether requests sent during the compaction will be retried automatically, or should our client implement retries?

We’ll try to drain any long-running sessions before 09:30 and run the verification steps after 10:00.

—Sam (Acme Ops)
ops@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acmecorp.com, infra@horizonai.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled stability safeguard activation and verification request

Hi Sam —

Short answers: this is a host-level allocator-mode toggle + in-memory compaction path. For Dedicated pools (ACME-POOL-3) we will apply the toggle in-place on the pool’s hosts; we do not expect full host reboots. If a host is unhealthy during the toggle, traffic will be routed off that host and you may see transient retries. Our runtime will attempt best-effort retries where requests are resumable; however, please ensure client-side idempotency for any operations that are not safe to duplicate.

Planned actions (operations playbook):
- 09:30 PT: start rolling toggles on 3 host batches (control plane-marked).
- 09:33–09:50 PT: progressive verification on live telemetry (latency 50p/95p, memory RSS, OOM counts).
- 09:50 PT: increase batch size if no regressions are observed.
- 10:00 PT: final sweep, publish completion.

What we’ll ask you to validate after 10:00 PT (also in attached verification_steps.txt):
1) Run: grep -E "(OOM|out_of_memory|kalloc_fail)" /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | tail -n 50
2) Check 95p latency against last 30m baseline (we’ll provide a dashboard link in the ticket).
3) Call the health-check endpoint for a representative route (URL in verification_steps.txt).

Fallbacks: if we observe elevated 5xx > 0.5% for >5 minutes during a batch, we’ll rollback automatically and promote a mitigation flag that applies stricter isolation on the pool.

I’ll post start/complete markers to INC-9981. If you hit any immediate issues during the window, DM me on Slack and we’ll pull a remote session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Update — completed and follow-up steps.

Status: The rolling safeguard activation completed at ~10:15 PT for ACME-POOL-3 after a brief additional validation batch. We observed no customer-impacting OOMs or sustained 5xx spikes. A small number of in-flight requests (estimated <0.1%) received retried responses; those were retried transparently by our runtime.

Actions we completed: 
- Applied allocator-mode toggle and compaction path to ACME-POOL-3 hosts.
- Ran progressive telemetry checks and a final sweep (all green).
- Uploaded hotfix notes and verification checklist to INC-9981.

Requested from Acme: please run the verification_steps.txt after you’ve had a chance and paste any grep results or dashboards to the ticket. If you confirm green, we’ll schedule a short postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis next week and share any long-term mitigations (allocator improvements, admission controls).

Thanks for the quick coordination and apologies again for the short notice. If you’d like immediate compensation for impact window (credits) please flag and I’ll escalate through Sales Ops.

Ben Carter
